rows.evidence: Q1: Section II (Materials and Methods) and Section III (Results) <U+2014> the authors collected 60 wheat leaves with aphid densities of 0<U+2013>120 per leaf from an experimental field in Beijing on 13 May 2011, measured leaf reflectance 350<U+2013>2500 nm with an ASD spectroradiometer and leaf clip, derived 48 spectral features by four methods, and built a PLSR model (validation R2 of 0.77, RMSE 15; Fig. 6).
rows.notes: The study only shows that leaf-level hyperspectral features (including the Aphid Index among 17 sensitive SFs, and a 5-feature PLSR model) correlate with and can estimate aphid density on individual, aphid-removed wheat leaves in a laboratory. It does not identify affected areas of a crop (no canopy, field or image data; authors state leaf-level analysis is only a first step toward canopy-level detection and that upscaling remains challenging), and it reports nothing on farmers taking action or on preventing further damage. The claimed effect (identification of affected areas enabling action to prevent damage / pest control) is downstream of what the study demonstrates (leaf-level detection), so Q2 is 'no' and the study is upstream. The authors do state limitations (leaf level only, aphids removed before measurement, single cultivar) and report RMSE, but these cannot be credited because Q2 is 'no'.

notes: Full text appears complete; some numerical values (coordinates, R2 thresholds, VIP values) are missing from the extracted text due to figure/equation rendering, but this does not affect the ratings.
